overview: Clorox is a multinational manufacturer and marketer of branded consumer and professional products, with fiscal year 2026 net sales of $6.7 billion generated across approximately 25 countries and 95 markets. Its portfolio includes Clorox, Pine-Sol, Glad, Fresh Step, Kingsford, Hidden Valley, Brita, Burt's Bees and, following the April 2026 acquisition of GOJO Industries, Purell; over 80% of sales come from brands holding the No. 1 or No. 2 share position in their categories. The business is organized into four reportable segments -- Health and Wellness, Household, Lifestyle and International -- and sells primarily through mass retailers, grocery, club and e-commerce channels, with Walmart alone representing roughly 26% of net sales.

business_model.summary: Clorox earns revenue almost entirely from sale of branded, repeat-purchase consumer packaged goods sold through mass retail, grocery, club and e-commerce channels in the U.S. (84% of FY2026 sales) and a smaller International segment (16%). The April 2026 GOJO (Purell) acquisition added a recurring B2B/institutional revenue stream built around an installed base of roughly 20 million dispensers, shifting the mix modestly toward business-to-business and healthcare/institutional customers.

revenue_streams.name: Health and Wellness (Clorox, Pine-Sol, Purell/GOJO, CloroxPro, Clorox Healthcare)
Household (Glad bags/wraps, Fresh Step/Scoop Away cat litter, Kingsford grilling)
Lifestyle (Hidden Valley food, Brita water filtration, Burt's Bees)
International (Clorox, Poett, Pine-Sol, Glad, Brita sold outside the U.S.)

business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2C through mass retailers, grocery, club, dollar and e-commerce channels; growing B2B/institutional exposure (healthcare, janitorial, food-service) via CloroxPro, Clorox Healthcare and the newly acquired GOJO/Purell distributor and dispenser network
business_model.geographic_mix: United States (including territories) ~84% of FY2026 net sales; International ~16%, with Latin America a meaningful contributor within International

competitive_position.market_position: Leading share positions (No. 1 or No. 2) in most of its core categories -- bleach/disinfecting, trash bags, cat litter, charcoal, salad dressing, water filtration -- but operates in mature, highly penetrated U.S. categories with intense private-label and multinational competition; Purell gives it the #1 position in hand sanitizer across both retail and B2B/institutional channels

moat_factors.description: Over 80% of sales from No. 1/No. 2 share brands; decades of trust in categories like bleach and disinfecting where brand drives purchase decisions

moat_factors.factor: Installed base / switching costs in B2B dispensing
moat_factors.description: GOJO/Purell's ~20 million installed dispensers and recurring consumable refill purchases create a sticky, recurring B2B revenue stream
Direct sales force and broker network reaching mass retailers, grocery and club channels; five largest customers ~50% of sales gives negotiating leverage but also customer concentration risk
EPA/FDA registration requirements for disinfecting and sanitizing products create some barrier to entry for new competitors in core categories

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on a small number of mature, highly competitive U.S. categories (84% of sales) with limited volume growth
High customer concentration -- Walmart alone is ~26% of net sales, five largest customers ~50%
Vulnerable to private-label and value-brand trade-down, especially during inflationary or recessionary periods
Scale is small relative to multinational competitors (P&G, Reckitt, Unilever) with greater financial resources for advertising and innovation
Recent execution missteps (cyberattack, ERP transition) show operational fragility relative to larger, more diversified peers

growth_drivers: GOJO/Purell acquisition expanding Health and Wellness into B2B health and hygiene with a large recurring dispenser installed base
IGNITE strategy innovation pipeline (Clorox PURE, Clorox Screen+ Sanitizing Wipes, Fresh Step Lightweight Litter, Glad ForceFlex MaxStrength, new Burt's Bees lip/body care)
Completion of the multi-year, ~$580 million ERP/digital transformation, expected to improve supply chain efficiency and support margin recovery
Full ownership of the Glad business following the P&G joint-venture buyout, enabling independent control of strategy, pricing and innovation
Pricing/cost-savings programs intended to rebuild gross margin back toward historical levels (~42% guided for FY2027) after inflation-driven declines
Expansion in institutional/B2B channels (healthcare, food-service) that are less exposed to private-label trade-down than traditional retail

business.description: Mature U.S. categories face aggressive private-label and value-brand competition, especially as macro pressure pushes consumers toward lower-priced alternatives
Walmart ~26% of net sales and five largest customers ~50%; loss of or reduced purchasing from a key retailer could materially hurt sales
Integrating a B2B-oriented acquisition with a different margin profile, distribution model and customer base alongside Clorox's consumer business creates channel-conflict and execution risk

Linda Rendle is stepping down for health reasons effective January 5, 2027; incoming CEO Fabian Garcia (ex-Revlon, ex-Unilever, ex-Colgate) must execute the IGNITE strategy and GOJO integration without disruption

financial.description: Debt rose to ~$5.1 billion after the ~$2.15 billion debt-financed GOJO acquisition and ~$476 million cash purchase of P&G's 20% Glad stake; S&P downgraded Clorox's long-term credit rating to BBB from BBB+ in February 2026
Total Clorox stockholders' equity was negative $39 million as of September 30, 2026, reflecting years of share buybacks and now rising debt
Interest expense more than doubled year-over-year (Q1 FY2027: $52M vs $23M) due to acquisition-related borrowing
A downgrade below investment grade would allow derivative counterparties to demand full collateralization and could raise borrowing costs and impair supply-chain financing

regulatory.description: GOJO acquisition adds cosmetics and OTC drug products subject to distinct, evolving FDA requirements
$28 million recorded environmental remediation liability; ongoing exposure related to historical sites and chlorine handling/transport
New and increased U.S. tariffs on imports, plus uncertainty from the ongoing USMCA joint review, raise input costs and complicate sourcing
Expanding state-level extended producer responsibility and plastics packaging rules could raise compliance costs

macro.risk: Consumer spending pressure and category slowdown
macro.description: Persistent macro uncertainty and elevated prices have driven category slowdowns, lower household penetration growth and cautious consumer shopping behavior in FY2026
Management guided to more than $200 million of inflation in FY2027, over double the historical $75-100 million range, driven by resins, chemicals, packaging and transportation costs
Conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East (including Iran), and China-Taiwan tensions, create supply chain, freight and commodity cost volatility
International segment (16% of sales) exposed to currency fluctuation, particularly in Latin America

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. household/personal care staples are a low-single-digit volume growth, mature industry; growth is driven mainly by pricing, mix and innovation rather than category expansion, with private label continuing to gain share during inflationary periods
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low to moderate - consumer staples demand is relatively defensive, but trade-down to private label and pantry-destocking cycles (as seen in FY2026) can meaningfully swing results
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate and rising - debt load increased materially after the debt-financed GOJO acquisition, making interest expense and refinancing costs more sensitive to rate levels

recent_developments.event: Filed Q1 FY2027 10-Q: net sales rose 33% YoY to $1,905M and diluted EPS rose to $1.39 from $0.65, driven by the GOJO acquisition and easy comparisons against prior-year ERP-related shipment timing distortions; gross margin declined 130bps to 40.4% on higher commodity and logistics costs

Board appointed Fabian Garcia (former Revlon CEO; former Unilever and Colgate-Palmolive executive) as the next CEO, effective January 5, 2027; Linda Rendle to step down as CEO and director, remaining in an advisory role through April 2027

Reported Q4 and full fiscal-year 2026 results: FY2026 net sales fell 5% to $6.72B, diluted EPS fell 26% to $4.81, gross margin declined to 42.3% from 45.2%; issued FY2027 guidance of 13-14% net sales growth (including ~9.5 points from GOJO), diluted EPS of $5.41-5.71, adjusted EPS of $5.70-6.00, and a ~42% gross margin target, with FY2027 inflation guided above $200 million
CEO and Chair Linda Rendle announced she asked the Board to begin a CEO succession search for health reasons, triggering an approximately 6% single-day stock decline

Completed acquisition of GOJO Industries (Purell) for approximately $2.15 billion in cash, funded with new debt and commercial paper; GOJO now operates as Clorox Purell (ProCare) within the Health and Wellness segment
Purchased Procter & Gamble's 20% interest in the Glad joint venture for $476 million following the January 31, 2026 expiration of the venture agreement, giving Clorox full ownership of Glad
S&P Global Ratings downgraded Clorox's long-term credit rating to BBB from BBB+, citing increased leverage from recent strategic transactions

Completed the multi-year ERP system replacement (core U.S. operations), the final phase of a ~$580 million digital transformation begun in fiscal 2022; completion caused temporary order-to-cash and inventory disruption in FY2026
Completed divestiture of the Better Health Vitamins, Minerals and Supplements (VMS) business, recording a loss on sale that weighed on prior-year comparisons

guidance.as_of: Q4/FY2026 Earnings (August 3, 2026); reaffirmed context in Q1 FY2027 10-Q (November 2, 2026)

items.notes: Includes approximately 9.5 points of benefit from the GOJO acquisition; organic sales growth guided at 3.5% to 4.5%
Implies 12-19% YoY growth off FY2026's $4.81, aided by GOJO contribution and easier comparisons
Implies 3-8% YoY growth; guided below some sell-side consensus estimates (~$6.0-6.2), reflecting a cautious framing
Cost savings expected to be more than offset by higher-than-normal inflation (>$200M, vs. historical $75-100M range) and unfavorable mix
Consistent with Clorox's longstanding targeted free cash flow range; FY2026 adjusted free cash flow was $881M (13.1% of net sales)

items.target: Weaker Q1 relative to full-year shape
items.notes: Management flagged Kingsford grilling seasonality timing and promotional activity would weigh on the first quarter; actual Q1 results (33% net sales growth, EPS of $1.39) came in strong, aided by GOJO and easy prior-year comparisons

guidance.management_commentary: Management continues to frame the operating environment as volatile and challenging, citing macro uncertainty, tariffs, and geopolitical instability (including the Iran conflict) as risks to consumer spending and input costs. The GOJO acquisition is positioned as central to reducing earnings volatility, accelerating sales growth and structurally improving margins over time. The CEO transition (Rendle to Garcia, effective January 2027) introduces near-term uncertainty around strategic continuity even as the Board frames it as an orderly, long-planned succession.

bull_case: GOJO/Purell acquisition adds a large recurring B2B revenue stream (installed base of ~20 million dispensers) and diversifies Clorox away from pure retail/private-label competition
FY2027 guidance implies a return to double-digit reported net sales growth and EPS recovery after a difficult FY2026 marred by ERP disruption and tough comparisons
Full ownership of Glad (post P&G buyout) gives Clorox complete strategic and pricing control over a meaningful, previously constrained business line
Over 80% of sales come from No. 1/No. 2 share brands, supporting pricing power and shelf-space resilience even in a competitive retail environment
Completion of the ~$580 million ERP/digital transformation removes a multi-year source of operational disruption and should support margin and supply-chain efficiency gains going forward
bear_case: Leverage increased materially to fund GOJO and the Glad buyout, pushing stockholders' equity negative and triggering an S&P downgrade to BBB, raising financial risk and borrowing costs
FY2027 guidance for >$200 million of inflation (vs. a historical $75-100 million range) and only ~42% gross margin signals persistent margin pressure, not a clean recovery
CEO transition (Rendle departing for health reasons, successor Fabian Garcia starting January 2027) adds leadership uncertainty during a complex acquisition integration
Core U.S. categories remain mature and exposed to private-label trade-down amid consumer spending pressure, tariffs and elevated prices

High customer concentration (Walmart ~26%, top five ~50% of sales) leaves Clorox vulnerable to retailer-driven pricing or shelf-space decisions, and sell-side sentiment has been cautious with several price-target cuts and hold/sell-leaning ratings through much of 2026
